DEFECT: functional hro_mgr_other_job (judge.toml:164) is scored 'Fails if accepted' but hro_observer_readonly (judge.toml:173) says 'the Observer is offered no move, add-candidate or note control ... Fails if any is offered or accepted', and functional prompt.md:43 instructs 'confirm no move, add or note control is offered'. No public sentence requires the UI to hide or withhold controls from the Observer: rules:18 'Observer | reads ...; changes nothing', rules:73 'An observer and a candidate move nothing', rules:21 'A signed-in caller whose role does not reach an action gets 403', rules:53 'A refused move changes nothing'. These are outcome rules satisfied by a server refusal. The task itself treats offered-but-refused as acceptable for another role (hro_mgr_other_job fails only 'if accepted'; hro_notes accepts 'not offered ... or is refused'), so the Observer 'offered' fail condition is a hidden UI requirement (REVIEW_POLICY 'No hidden requirements'; 'every graded demand needs a public requirement'). Same pattern, weaker, in hro_thread_access (judge.toml:362) 'the Observer reads it with no way to send. Fails if any access differs' vs rules:133 'write in none' - a visible send box whose send is refused could be read as a 'way to send'. SECONDARY NOTES (not independently blocking): (a) polish hro_pol_failed_send (polish judge.toml:50) requires 'A visible explanation appears' for a failed send, while rules:140 says only 'A message that could not be sent stays in the box'; its Fails-if clause does not list a missing explanation, so the risk is judge inconsistency, not a certain wrong score - the brief's 'tell me why' (instruction.md:3) covers refused moves, not sends. (b) render gate hro_gate_render (render judge.toml:23) requires a visible refusal for a wrong password; not stated, but password sign-in is stated (instruction.md:17, rules:11) and a visible wrong-password refusal is house convention for the stated sign-in surface; Note only. (c) 'not offered' wording in hro_move_one_stage/hro_reject_hired/hro_mgr_early_refused is harmless because their Fails-if clauses only fail on acceptance and prompt.md:23 handles the not-offered path. No runtime/judge run was used or needed; this verdict is a source-level reading.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that fails: an app renders one shared board UI for all staff, so the Observer Aud Halvorsen sees the same 'Move to Screen', 'Add candidate' and 'Add note' buttons as recruiters; every click as Aud returns 403 with 'Observers cannot change anything', the card/note/candidate list is unchanged, and no activity line is added. This satisfies rules:18, 21, 53, 73 and 113 exactly, yet hro_observer_readonly fails ('Fails if any is offered'), and a judge may also fail hro_thread_access because the Observer sees a send box (refused on send). A plausible weaker app that hides controls but still accepts an Observer replay would correctly fail via the replay half, so the 'offered' clause adds no discrimination the replay does not already provide.
suggested_fix: Either state the requirement publicly (e.g. add to hireops_rules.md s1/s3: 'The observer's screens offer no move, add-candidate, note or send controls') or change hro_observer_readonly to 'Fails if any request is accepted or changes anything' (matching hro_mgr_other_job) and the R protocol line to 'record whether controls are offered', and make hro_thread_access's Observer clause 'cannot send (no send control, or a send is refused with nothing added)'.
